pages.text: A permanent magnet holds its field only so hot. Past the temperature it is rated to, the field sags, and comes back as it cools. Further on, part of it is lost for good. At its Curie point it is gone.
pages.title: Magnets and heat

pages.text: The Factory's motors, generators, stators, electric pumps and voltmeters are built round one grade of magnet and carry it: the item says which, and goggles on the block give the grade, the temperature where it stands (the field the thermometers read) and the share of full output it makes.

In the game, every few seconds: NdFeB Magnet: rated 80 °C, lasting loss past 120, Curie 320, 100% strength. Dy-NdFeB Magnet: rated 180 °C, lasting loss past 230, Curie 340, 100% strength. SmCo Magnet: rated 300 °C, lasting loss past 400, Curie 800, 80% strength.
pages.title: The grades

pages.text: Alnico Magnet: rated 525 °C, lasting loss past 600, Curie 860, 40% strength. Steel Magnet: rated 150 °C, lasting loss past 250, Curie 770, 25% strength.

Output falls from full at the rating to half at the lasting-loss point and to nothing at Curie; a motor turns slower and carries less, a generator gives less, an electric pump pushes less. A demagnetised machine stops. A voltmeter's needle swings against its magnet, so it reads low by what the heat has taken of its field.

The first magnet is hardened carbon steel. Heat a steel ingot in a furnace and quench the hot steel under a spout with 250 mB of water. In an unpowered steel vat, combine copper, zinc, a glass bottle, 50 mB of sulfuric acid and 200 mB of water into a galvanic cell.
pages.title: First electricity

pages.text: Craft the cell, hardened steel and copper wire together: the cell's current magnetizes the steel. The recipe consumes the cell and winding. This is a 25% starter magnet; its game heat limits are 150, 250 and 770 °C. The cell does not drive the factory. Mechanical rotation drives its generator.

An ordinary iron ingot can be the unfinished coil's core, and iron plates can be the transformer's laminations. Wind the coils mechanically. Silicon steel is useful core material, but is not a prerequisite for induction. Transform the generator's output, never the cell's steady DC.
pages.title: To the arc furnace

pages.text: Three graphite electrodes make the first silicon. Each needs at least 1,500 volts and 7,500 watts in The Factory's model; keep each on its own small-transformer output and supply enough generation upstream. Watch current as well as voltage: raising voltage also raises load.

The real figures, from the makers' grade tables: sintered NdFeB runs to about 80 °C, Curie point 310 to 400 °C. With dysprosium or terbium (the SH, UH and EH grades) it runs to 150 to 230 °C. SmCo runs to 250 to 350 °C, Curie 720 to 825.
pages.title: Why it matters

pages.text: Alnico runs to 450 to 550 °C, Curie about 860, but stores far less energy: about 5 MGOe, against 35 to 52 for NdFeB and 16 to 32 for SmCo.

So aircraft and missiles fly SmCo, alnico lives on in sensors, and every other motor is NdFeB with dysprosium for the heat, which is most of why the world wants dysprosium (US Department of Energy, Critical Materials Strategy, 2011).

Plain NdFeB is two neodymium, three iron and a ferroboron under argon; three neodymium, a dysprosium or terbium, six iron and two ferroboron make eight Dy-NdFeB. SmCo is two samarium, four cobalt, an iron and four copper and two zirconium nuggets, the Sm2Co17 type every high-temperature grade is.
pages.title: Making them

pages.text: Alnico is iron with aluminium, nickel, cobalt and a little copper: five iron, an aluminium, two nickel, two cobalt and three copper nuggets, superheated, cast and heat-treated to ten ingots. Polarize any of the four ingots, or an NdFeB, Dy-NdFeB or SmCo plate, to its magnet.
The magnet is the first thing a motor or generator takes on the belt, and it decides the grade of the whole: a motor is begun on a shaft, a generator on a steel plate.

A motor, generator, stator, electric pump or voltmeter and any magnet in a crafting grid rebuild it round that magnet, at full field: that is how a cooked or demagnetised machine comes back, or a cheap one is upgraded.
pages.title: Rebuilding

pages.text: Machines built before grades, and The Factory Must Grow's own magnets still in a chest, count as Dy-NdFeB, which is what every NdFeB the mod made then was. The Factory's magnet is no longer made.
The horseshoe: cast alnico, painted red, its two poles bare.
